newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower in choppy trading.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower in choppy trading.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Friday in choppy trading as bearish sentiment overtook the market after an afternoon attempt to resume Thursday's recovery fizzled.
"People are turning bearish as futures became more in line with cash (prices)," said one New York futures broker.
Thursday's rally, led by shortcovering, failed to carry over into today's session.
The power complex suffered sharp losses earlier this week on concerns over rising generation and easing air-conditioning demand in the Southwest.
In the West, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 on the coast of central California and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 near Phoenix, Arizona, both reached full power early Friday after recent outages.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired plant and a 550 MW at the Laramie River Station, both in Wyoming, are expected to return online by industry sources said.

Meterologists said temperatures in the West would average near to slightly below normal through the weekend. In a six to 10 day outlook, readings across the region were forecast to run at to above seasonal levels.
July California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down 67 cents at $17.42 megawatt hour (MWh), erasing a 31 cent gain.
August COB finished down 35 cents at $22.07. Deferred COB months ended down two cents to up 40 cents.
July Palo Verde (PV) settled down 25 cents at $27.92 after posting a high at $28.30.
August PV finished unchanged at $31.11 after bouncing between $31.00 and $31.30. Other PV contracts ended down 31 cents to up 20 cents.
In the cash market, firm, peak electricity prices for Monday at COB slipped to $11.50-13.50 down from Thursday's $13.50-14.25, while those at PV fell to $21.00-23.00 from $22.50-23.50 yesterday.

Spot physical prices were under additional pressure when Bonneville Power Administration resumed offering daily peak, firm power today at $12.00 for Northwest delivery and $13.00 for COB sales. The agency did offer the product Thursday.
After a volatile week, market sources are uncertain about the short-term price direction of the complex.
"It tried to push up and down today. I wouldn't read too much into it yet," said a Houston futures trader.
NYMEX estimated 392 PV and 790 COB contracts were sold, well below yesterday's 1,021 PV and record 1,068 COB lots.
